43.summary: The Prince de Conti's mémoire for his envoy Geoffroy, marquis de Laigue, to Archduke Leopold Wilhelm, Paris, 5 March 1649: Laigue is to counter the cardinal's account of the conference the parlement had accepted, telling the archduke that the talks were caused only by his delay in sending help and that Conti's party keeps its word to work for peace between the two crowns by removing those who oppose it. The first twelve lines were never glossed and are decoded here; the rest follows the contemporary interlinear decipherment.
43.en:
For Monsieur de Laigue. Because we do not doubt that the Cardinal will put a bad interpretation on all their
actions, and that he will principally make his efforts to put the Archduke in distrust of our good intentions on the
subject of the conference which [the] Parlement has granted, I have thought fit to have you instructed of it, so that
you may turn aside the bad effects of the Cardinal's artifices, and make the Archduke understand that this parley was
caused and resolved only by the delays the Archduke brings to succouring us, and that we are still in our same
designs, without anything being able to alter the word we ha[ve given] to work strongly to procure for the two crowns
tranquillity and peace by the removal of those who oppose it.

system: Numeric letter-and-syllable code: four interleaved single-letter alphabets, five-syllable consonant blocks with a second homophonic series, underline reverses a syllable, nulls 99-250, a few code words.
